rationale: The agent verified the user correctly using full name and zip, matched to a single account, then accessed only that user’s data. It listed the user’s two orders and confirmed the shipping address change before performing any writes, updating both pending orders’ addresses successfully. For the jigsaw change, the agent clearly stated the intended action (switch to the easiest, least-pieces variant) and requested explicit confirmation including the payment method for any price difference. After the user confirmed PayPal, the agent checked product variants, updated the item to a 500-piece beginner option, and used the specified PayPal method; the tool output shows the order now contains that variant, implying the change succeeded and any price difference was handled. Information given to the user matches tool outputs. Minor quibbles: the agent stated order status as pending without an explicit status field in the displayed tool response and did not reconfirm the exact new variant before writing, and it did not proactively offer to update the profile address. However, these do not violate the policy’s pass bar: the agent authenticated properly, obtained confirmation before writes, performed correct changes, and provided accurate final information supported by the tools.
